commit.message:
feat(openai-base, ai-openrouter, ai-groq, ai-utils): send json_object when strict json_schema is rejected (#1775)

* feat(ai, openai-base, ai-openrouter, ai-groq): send json_object when strict json_schema is rejected

* refactor(openai-base, ai-openrouter, ai-groq, ai-utils): pick json_object in the adapter and send the schema as a system prompt

Drop the structuredOutputMode option from chat(). Adapters choose JSON mode
from modelOptions or the model catalog, and add the schema as a system
prompt because JSON mode does not send it.

* fix(openai-base, ai-openrouter): keep JSON mode off tool turns and match :variant catalog ids

- supportsCombinedToolsAndSchema() returns false in JSON mode, so the schema
  prompt goes only on the separate structured-output request. mapOptionsToRequest
  no longer adds it, so it cannot repeat.
- OpenRouter checks the full id (with modelOptions.variant) before the id
  without its :variant, in one shared helper for the JSON-only and combined sets.
- Docs, changeset and skills: plain JSON Schema and streamed replies are not
  validated; note the openai-base json_object behavior change.
- Tests: :free/variant/fallback lookup, combined gate in JSON mode, OpenRouter
  chat and Responses JSON mode with tools, single schema prompt, Groq prompt.

@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+---
+'@tanstack/ai-utils': minor
+'@tanstack/openai-base': minor
+'@tanstack/ai-openrouter': minor
+'@tanstack/ai-groq': minor
+---
+
+Structured output sends `response_format: { type: "json_object" }` for OpenRouter and Groq models that declare a response format without strict structured outputs. These models reject strict `json_schema`. In JSON mode the adapter adds the schema as a system prompt. `await chat({ outputSchema })` checks the reply when the schema is a Standard Schema, such as Zod. Other models keep strict `json_schema`.
+
+`modelOptions` can set `json_object` for any model. On the OpenAI-base adapters (OpenAI, Grok, Groq and others), a `json_object` in `modelOptions` was replaced by strict `json_schema`. It is now sent as given, with the schema in a system prompt. In JSON mode, `supportsCombinedToolsAndSchema()` returns `false`. Tools and the schema then go out in separate requests, so the tool-calling turns do not get the schema prompt.
+
+OpenRouter catalog ids with a `:variant`, such as `google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it:free`, now match their own catalog entry. Before, only the id without the variant was checked.

@@ -62,6 +62,39 @@ Every adapter handles structured output through its provider's native API:
 
 The provider-specific details are handled for you. The same `chat({ outputSchema })` call works across all of them. For a coding agent in a sandbox, see [Harness Agents](./harnesses).
 
+### When strict JSON schema is rejected
+
+Some models reject strict JSON schema. They accept JSON mode (`response_format` type `json_object`) only. A strict request to one of these models fails before the model runs.
+
+The OpenRouter and Groq adapters find these models in their catalogs. For these models, `chat({ outputSchema })` does two things:
+
+- It sends JSON mode.
+- It adds your schema to the system prompt, because JSON mode does not send the schema.
+
+When your schema is a Standard Schema, such as Zod, `await chat({ outputSchema })` still checks the reply. JSON of the wrong shape throws. TanStack AI does not check a plain JSON Schema or a streamed reply. Check those in your own code.
+
+```typescript
+import { chat } from "@tanstack/ai";
+import { openRouterText } from "@tanstack/ai-openrouter";
+import { z } from "zod";
+
+const Person = z.object({ name: z.string(), age: z.number() });
+
+const person = await chat({
+  adapter: openRouterText("qwen/qwen3.7-flash"),
+  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Return Ada Lovelace, age 36." }],
+  outputSchema: Person,
+});
+
+person.name;
+person.age;
+```
+
+To send JSON mode to a model that is not in the catalog, set it in `modelOptions`:
+
+- OpenRouter: `modelOptions: { responseFormat: { type: "json_object" } }`
+- Groq: `modelOptions: { response_format: { type: "json_object" } }`
+
 ### Anthropic schema complexity limits
 
 Anthropic compiles a structured-output schema into a grammar and rejects schemas it considers too large or too complex with a 400 error — typically `Schema is too complex for compilation` or `output_config.format.schema: Invalid schema: The compiled grammar is too large`. This affects Claude models directly and `anthropic/*` models routed through OpenRouter, even when every other provider accepts the same schema.

+import { jsonModeSystemPrompt } from '@tanstack/ai-utils'
+import { OPENROUTER_JSON_OBJECT_ONLY_MODELS } from '../model-meta'
+import { openRouterModelIn, openRouterRoutedModels } from './model-ids'
+import type { TextOptions } from '@tanstack/ai'
+
+/**
+ * True when this OpenRouter call must send `json_object`. The caller set it
+ * in `modelOptions` (`responseFormat` or `text.format`), or a routed model
+ * (`model` with its `variant`, or `modelOptions.models`) has
+ * `response_format` and not `structured_outputs` in the catalog.
+ */
+export function openRouterUsesJsonObject(
+  model: string,
+  modelOptions: unknown,
+): boolean {
+  const record = (modelOptions ?? {}) as {
+    responseFormat?: { type?: unknown }
+    text?: { format?: { type?: unknown } }
+  }
+  if (
+    record.responseFormat?.type === 'json_object' ||
+    record.text?.format?.type === 'json_object'
+  ) {
+    return true
+  }
+  return openRouterRoutedModels(model, modelOptions).some((id) =>
+    openRouterModelIn(OPENROUTER_JSON_OBJECT_ONLY_MODELS, id),
+  )
+}
+
+/** Add the schema as a system prompt, because JSON mode does not send it. */
+export function withJsonModePrompt<
+  TProviderOptions extends Record<string, any>,
+>(
+  options: TextOptions<TProviderOptions>,
+  schema: unknown,
+): TextOptions<TProviderOptions> {
+  return {
+    ...options,
+    systemPrompts: [
+      ...(options.systemPrompts ?? []),
+      jsonModeSystemPrompt(schema),
+    ],
+  }
+}

+/**
+ * The ids a call routes to: `model` with any `modelOptions.variant` suffix,
+ * then each `modelOptions.models` fallback.
+ */
+export function openRouterRoutedModels(
+  model: string,
+  modelOptions: unknown,
+): Array<string> {
+  const record = (modelOptions ?? {}) as { variant?: unknown; models?: unknown }
+  const primary =
+    typeof record.variant === 'string' && record.variant
+      ? `${model}:${record.variant}`
+      : model
+  const fallbacks = Array.isArray(record.models)
+    ? record.models.filter((id): id is string => typeof id === 'string')
+    : []
+  return [primary, ...fallbacks]
+}
+
+/**
+ * The catalog lists some `:variant` ids (for example `:free`) as their own
+ * models. Check the full id first, then the id without its `:variant`.
+ */
+export function openRouterModelIn(
+  set: ReadonlySet<string>,
+  id: string,
+): boolean {
+  if (set.has(id)) return true
+  const variantIndex = id.indexOf(':')
+  return variantIndex !== -1 && set.has(id.slice(0, variantIndex))
+}

+/**
+ * System prompt for JSON mode (`json_object`). JSON mode does not send the
+ * schema, so the prompt carries it. The prompt also has the word "JSON",
+ * which some providers require in JSON mode.
+ */
+export function jsonModeSystemPrompt(schema: unknown): string {
+  return `Respond with only a JSON object that matches this JSON Schema:\n${JSON.stringify(schema)}`
+}

+import { jsonModeSystemPrompt } from '@tanstack/ai-utils'
+import type { TextOptions } from '@tanstack/ai'
+
+/** Caller set JSON mode on a Chat Completions or Responses body. */
+export function explicitJsonObject(modelOptions: unknown): boolean {
+  if (modelOptions == null || typeof modelOptions !== 'object') return false
+  if ('response_format' in modelOptions) {
+    const format = (modelOptions as { response_format?: { type?: unknown } })
+      .response_format
+    if (format?.type === 'json_object') return true
+  }
+  if ('text' in modelOptions) {
+    const text = (modelOptions as { text?: { format?: { type?: unknown } } })
+      .text
+    if (text?.format?.type === 'json_object') return true
+  }
+  return false
+}
+
+/** Add the schema as a system prompt, because JSON mode does not send it. */
+export function withJsonModePrompt<
+  TProviderOptions extends Record<string, any>,
+>(
+  options: TextOptions<TProviderOptions>,
+  schema: unknown,
+): TextOptions<TProviderOptions> {
+  return {
+    ...options,
+    systemPrompts: [
+      ...(options.systemPrompts ?? []),
+      jsonModeSystemPrompt(schema),
+    ],
+  }
+}
